text:
Alex: Heads-up — were planning to replace X-Redwood-Route with a new compact header X-RW-Route-Attrs and start returning 400 when the header is malformed. Need SDK impact assessment (py/ts/go) + console telemetry migration ideas.
Maya: :eyes: can you paste the intended schema?
Alex: example: `X-RW-Route-Attrs: {"tenant":"acme","policy":"cost","route_id":"r-12","quota_bucket":"b-9","sample_rate":0.02}` — compact JSON, fewer ad-hoc fields.
Sam: This will break clients that relied on implicit old-header passthrough. We should plan SDK-side compatibility shims.
Maya: For the Python SDK I propose an opt-in env var RW_MIGRATE_ROUTE_HEADER=1 that turns on legacy parsing->new header conversion. Warn in logs once per process.
Jen: Backend note: we plan to start strict validation in 14 days (will reject malformed/unknown keys). We can emit a deprecation header to clients for a short window.
Liam: For TS/Go SDKs we can add a client option `routeHeaderMode: "strict" | "compat" | "auto"`. In `auto` we parse legacy X-Redwood-Route and set X-RW-Route-Attrs when missing.
Sam: Auto-conversion is convenient but might mask server-side issues. Suggest default `auto` but log a soft warning and expose opt-out.
Maya: Streaming note: the Python streaming client currently accepts mid-stream route hint updates via headers; need to ensure we don't drop or reorder those when converting. Add unit tests.
Alex: Console telemetry: dashboards currently attribute by `route` extracted from the old header. We need consistent attribution to `route_id` coming from the new header. Migration will impact cost dashboards and quota rollups.
Jen: Ops plan — we'll publish a migration mapping endpoint `/internal/route-map` that returns legacyKey->canonicalRouteId. Console pulls it daily to reconcile historical data.
Sam: Need e2e tests: SDKs + staging backend + console ingest to validate no regressions in quota dashboards.
CI Bot: deploy-bot: Canary: route-header-migration v1.0 promoted to staging at 2026-03-21T10:12Z
Maya: I'll open py-sdk PR (will include env var, `routeHeaderMode` client arg, and a migration unit test against staging).
Liam: I'll handle the TS/Go shims and add an integration test that toggles header modes.
Jen: Ops — prepare a rollback playbook if we see >1% increase in client 4xxs after rollout. Also add a temporary alert for any spike in header-parsing errors.
Sam: Also update SDK changelogs and a short migration doc in devex: quick code snippets for switching to `routeHeaderMode='compat'` and how to opt into migration.
Alex: Proposed timeline: SDK compatibility patches out in 5 days, server deprecation header turned on in 14 days, hard 400 enforcement in 30 days.
Maya: Sounds good. I'll tag folks on the PR.
Liam: I'll queue the TS/Go PRs and tests.
Jen: +1 — will create the ops runbook and the /internal/route-map stub.
Sam: No objections from me.
Alex: If no objections by EOD well proceed with this timeline. :thumbsup:
Maya: quick question — do we want a one-time console migration job to rewrite old historical rows to use route_id? That could avoid confusing dashboards.
Jen: Yes, but need data owner sign-off. I'll route to analytics.
Sam: Also callout: document expected user-facing errors so support can triage (400 payload, 422 if missing route_id).
Maya: PR opened: py-sdk #482 (WIP) — includes migration flag and unit tests.
CI Bot: deploy-bot: Note: staging canary logs are available at https://staging-logs.example.com/route-migration
Alex: Great work everyone — keeping this minimal-impact but explicit is the goal.
